newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures narrowly mixed, await NAPM data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures narrowly mixed, await NAPM data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were narrowly mixed early as bond and Eurodollar traders awaited key U.S. June National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) data at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
They said some dealers upwardly revised estimates for the NAPM index after the Chicagoland NAPM index rose more than expected for June.
According to a Reuters poll, dealers on average are looking for June NAPM to fall to 56.4 from 57.1 in May. Chicago's NAPM, which was released Monday, rose to 61.5 from 56.8 in May.
One futures trader said the new orders component will be significant in gauging the rate of U.S. economic growth in the latter half of the second quarter.

"If consumer demand is starting to pick-up again you would expect to see it in new orders," he said. "Prices and supplier deliveries will lag, but if gains in new orders persist you would expect to see those components start to rise."
Traders said the BTM/Schroders weekly U.S. chain store sales data was soft and initially helped keep September T-bonds above 111-02/32.
BTM/Schroders index for the week ended June 28 was up 0.1 percent from the previous week.
However, traders said a round of selling by several dealers pushed September to 110-30/32. The two-week low of 110-23/32 was set Monday.

Further support is at 110-15/32, a one-thirds retracement level from the contract's 2-1/2-month rally. One trader said the chart would turn negative if September broke through the three-week low of 110-12/32.
December Eurodollars carved out an even narrower trading range from Monday. Support is at 93.85.
Nervousness about the FOMC's two-day meeting, which begins Tuesday, was nonexistent. Traders said the market is fairly priced for no Fed rate hike at the conclusion of the FOMC meeting on Wednesday.
"The Fed is betting on a slowdown in growth," a Eurodollar futures trader said.
U.S. May leading economic indicators (LEI) and U.S. May construction spending will also be released at 1000 EDT/1400 GTM. LEI is forecast to rise 0.2 percent, from April's decline of 0.1 percent.
Construction spending is expected to rise 0.5 percent in May, from down 1.0 percent in April.

At 0837 CDT/1337 GMT, September T-bonds were flat at 111-02/32, December Eurodollars were off 0.005 at 93.895 and 10-year T-notes were off 01/32 at 107-27/32. ((Chicago Derivatives Desk (312) 408-8750))
